name: AI lead qualification with a confidence gate (Claude + deterministic routing)

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({"model": "claude-opus-5", "max_tokens": 512, "system": "You qualify inbound B2B leads. Return a structured assessment only.

lead_score (0-100): how well this lead fits an ideal customer — a real, concrete need plus the size and budget to act on it.

confidence (0-1): how much your READING of this enquiry can be relied on — NOT how good the lead is. A short, vague or ambiguous message means low confidence even if you had to pick a score. This is used to decide whether a salesperson's time is spent, so report it honestly.

Judge only what the enquiry says. Never invent budget, headcount or urgency.", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": $json.leadText}], "output_config": {"effort": "low", "format": {"type": "json_schema", "schema": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["lead_score", "confidence", "reason", "industry"], "properties": {"lead_score": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 100}, "confidence": {"type": "number", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 1}, "reason": {"type": "string"}, "industry": {"type": "string"}}}}}}) }}

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ route: $json.route, lead_score: $json.lead_score, confidence: $json.confidence, applied_rule: $json.applied_rule, next_action: $json.next_action }) }}

parameters.content:
## The idea: the model proposes, deterministic rules decide

Most AI lead-qualification workflows let the model output "hot / warm / cold" and act on it directly. That is not reproducible: the same lead can classify differently between runs, and a model upgrade silently re-routes your whole funnel.

Here Claude returns only a **score** and a **confidence**. The **Deterministic routing** Code node decides the route from those two numbers. Edit the thresholds there — that node is your business policy, and it is the only thing that chooses an outcome.

## Two gates, not one — and why low confidence never archives

**Score** says how good the lead looks. **Confidence** says how much the model's *reading* of the enquiry can be relied on. They are different questions, and only the second one tells you whether to spend a person's hour.

A lead must clear **both** gates for its tier. Clearing the score but not the confidence drops it **exactly one tier — never straight to archive.**

That asymmetry is deliberate: a sales call costs an hour, a nurture sequence costs almost nothing, and archiving is the only outcome you cannot undo. So a score of 95 the model is 55% sure about goes to nurture, not to sales and not to the bin.

## Setup

1. Add an **Anthropic** credential to this node (API key from console.anthropic.com).
2. Point your form / CRM webhook at the **Receive lead** URL.
3. Replace the three **NoOp** nodes with your own actions — HubSpot, GoHighLevel, Pipedrive, Slack, whatever you use.

The model is set to `claude-opus-5`. Swap it for `claude-sonnet-5` or `claude-haiku-4-5` in the request body if you want a cheaper run per lead — the routing logic is unchanged.

**Note the parsing in the Code node.** The Messages API returns `content[0].text`, not your fields at the top level. Reading `$json.lead_score` directly is the mistake that makes every lead score 0.
